newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq attacks Kuwait, Saudi for Western flights.
newsitem.headline: Iraq attacks Kuwait, Saudi for Western flights.

text.p: Iraq holds Kuwait and Saudi Arabia accountable for damage caused by U.S., British and French warplanes during their patrols of southern Iraq, Foreign Minister Mohammed Saeed al-Sahaf said in a statement published in newspapers on Monday.

They said Sahaf had sent the statement to Arab League Secretary-General Esmat Abdel Meguid in which he protested against the use of Saudi and Kuwaiti bases for flights by Western aircrafts over its territory.

"Iraq holds Saudi Arabia and Kuwait full international responsibility for the damages inflicted by American, British and French planes which violated its airspace by using Saudi and Kuwaiti bases as a launching pad," Sahaf said in the statement.
Warplanes from the three countries police two no-fly zones in Iraq - one in the north to protect Kurds from possible military attacks by Baghdad and the second in the south.

Sahaf said the Western planes made 740 sorties in the first half of November and urged Abdel Meguid to interfere with the Saudi and Kuwaiti authorities to put an end "to these violations which contravene the joint defence pact between Arab countries."
Iraq issues regular protests against Western violations of its airspace but it was the first time it said it would hold Saudi Arabia and Kuwait responsible for damage.
Iraq invaded Kuwait in 1990. A U.S.-led multinational force, using Saudi Arabia as a springboard, drove Iraqi troops out of Kuwait in 1991.
Sahaf did not specify the kind of damage the flights have caused to Iraq.
